$comment: Where the launcher's state home is: the directory that holds tokens.json (and the launcher's own stack.json and discovery/kbs.json). Every program that finds those files computes it the same way. `os` is `macos`, `windows`, or anything else; `home` is the home directory (HOME, or USERPROFILE on Windows), `xdgStateHome` is XDG_STATE_HOME, and `localAppData` is LOCALAPPDATA; null, or a key a case leaves out, means not set. `dir` null means there is no state home, and nothing is read or written. `dir` is written with the system's own separator, whatever system computes it: a backslash on Windows, a slash elsewhere. Rust (packages/sdk-rust: sign_in_store::state_dir) runs every case; it is given what the environment says and reads none itself. The launcher's Go (apps/launcher/internal/launcher: stateDirFor) runs every case too, and StateDir reads the environment for it.

cases.why: elsewhere, XDG_STATE_HOME when it is set
an empty XDG_STATE_HOME is one that is not set
with no home there is no state home, even where XDG_STATE_HOME is set
an empty home is no home
macOS with no home has no state home
Windows follows LOCALAPPDATA where it is not under the home
Windows, when LOCALAPPDATA is not set: where it is by default, under the home
an empty LOCALAPPDATA is one that is not set
Windows with no home has no state home, even where LOCALAPPDATA is set
